Course Title: Advanced Database Management System (Distributed Database Systems)
description: To develop understanding of distributed database design and query processing.

syllabus.title: Introduction and Distributed Database Design
syllabus.body: What is a Distributed Database System? Data delivery alternatives, promises of DDBSs, design issues, distributed DBMS architecture. Data fragmentation, allocation, combined approaches, adaptive approaches, data directory.

syllabus.title: Distributed Data Control
syllabus.body: View management, access control, and semantic integrity control.

syllabus.title: Distributed Query Processing
syllabus.body: Overview, data localization, join ordering in distributed queries, distributed cost model, distributed query optimization, adaptive query processing.

syllabus.title: Distributed Transaction Processing
syllabus.body: Background and terminology, distributed query control, distributed concurrency control using snapshot isolation, distributed DBMS reliability, modern approaches to scaling out transaction management.

syllabus.title: Data Replication
syllabus.body: Consistency of replicated databases, update management strategies, replication protocols, group communication, replication and failures.

outcomes: To comprehend issues and solutions of distributed databases.
To develop understanding of design and implementation of distributed databases.
textbooks: M. Tamer Özsu and Patrick Valduriez, Principles of Distributed Database Systems, Fourth Edition, Springer.
